comment: The vectors pinning Prima.WorkerAuth and Prima.Assignment: the suite derives every key here from the root, the worker service id and the attempt, reproduces every canonical string, header, MAC, sealed value and assignment token from the fields and fixed IVs, opens every sealed value, and decodes every valid root text to the root and refuses every invalid one. Integers are written in decimal in canonical strings, headers and key labels. The service id is the key input; the boot is signed beside it and compared, never derived over. The member is the control-plane member that issued the assignment and answers that attempt's host calls: a call header field, an assignment field beside host_url (the address those calls are posted to) and an argument of the exit report. A member that is not the one named refuses the call, whatever it asked for. This file holds the primitives only: the messages of the wire, sealed and signed with these keys, are tests/fixtures/host_api.json's and tests/fixtures/worker_api.json's, and a status answer's vectors are worker_api.json's. sealed_frames are the frames of one attached request's answer for call_id: each a kind byte in clear and the plaintext sealed with the attempt seal key under label with call_id, seq and kind as fields, from iv_hex; frame_hex is the frame as it crosses, its 4-byte length first. assignment_reads are tokens a worker reads without the assign key (Prima.Assignment.read/1): each valid token reads as its payload, every member of it, an absent optional member read as none, and each invalid one is refused with its reason, malformed or unknown_version. A token is the base64url of the payload and of a MAC, both unpadded, re-encoding to itself; its MAC is not checked. A member given twice is its first, and every integer member is at most 2^53 − 1, the greatest integer the runner's wires hold: one past it is refused. The Rust runner's crate reads them too, and the cases are those both read alike: the crate holds actor and authority as JSON objects it does not read further (Prima.Actor and Prima.Authority's own rules are CYFR's at attach), and a component's type and the canonical form of its ref likewise, so no case here turns on what they hold; a component without its type is refused by both. headers are host-call, WorkerAPI request and report headers (kind), each verified at now under the key that verifies its kind: a call under the attempt call key, as a worker service verifies its runner's call before it posts it (Prima.WorkerAuth.verify_host_call_header_under/3), a request under the dispatch key (verify_request_header/3) and a report under the root (verify_report_header/3); accepted ones answer their fields and body_hash, refused ones error, malformed or unknown_version, which is each kind's grammar: a version token other than v1 first, then exactly v1 and name=value pairs separated by one space, kind and every field once, body and mac, in any order, an integer in decimal without a sign or a leading zero and at most 2^53 - 1, every value 1 to 256 bytes of printable ASCII. verify are headers whose refusal is decided past the grammar, in the order Prima.WorkerAuth documents: unknown_version, malformed, outside_window (more than 30,000 ms from now on either side; at 30,000 it verifies), bad_mac. body_checks are bodies checked against the hash a verified header named (verify_body/2), another body being bad_mac. open_attempt_keys are sealed attempt keys each opened with the dispatch seal key (open_attempt_keys/2), to the attempt and keys they name, or unsealable; open_call are host-call halves each opened as direction of call (open_call/4), to their plaintext, or unsealable. A sealed value or a name in it reads its base64url unpadded or with its padding, bits past the last byte ignored. A case marked go is the two ends' stated difference, each side's test asserting its own answer: Prima reads a name of any depth, and a Go reader refuses one nested past 4,096 before it parses it (go's error). assignment_service_reads are tokens a worker service reads where the crate, holding actor and authority unread, reads otherwise: refused are tokens Prima.Assignment.read/1 refuses malformed, and a worker service with it, in a member it reads (a component's type or reference not canonical, an authority's cursor, bound node's limits or egress); read are tokens both read; carried are tokens Prima refuses for their actor, or for a part of their authority a worker service does not read, which a worker service reads and carries, and CYFR refuses when the runner attaches. A read token marked go is the two ends' stated difference: Prima reads a payload of any depth, and a Go reader refuses one nested past 4,096 (go's error).
